title: Missa Salisburgensis
description: A huge Mass for 53 voices and instruments, written for the 1,100th anniversary of the archbishopric in 1682 and long credited to others. Biber, the archbishop’s music director, placed choirs and trumpets around the cathedral.

title: Divertimento in D major, K. 136
description: One of three bright pieces for strings that Mozart wrote in Salzburg at 16, between trips to Italy. They are sometimes called the Salzburg Symphonies.

title: Coronation Mass, K. 317
description: Mozart wrote this Mass in 1779, back in Salzburg as cathedral organist after a failed job hunt in Paris. It was probably first heard at Easter in the cathedral, where he had been baptized.

title: Stille Nacht, heilige Nacht
description: “Silent Night,” with words by the priest Joseph Mohr and music by the teacher Franz Xaver Gruber, first sung with a guitar on Christmas Eve 1818 in Oberndorf, north of Salzburg. It is now sung in hundreds of languages.

title: Do-Re-Mi
description: Rodgers and Hammerstein’s song for teaching the scale, from the film of The Sound of Music. The sequence ends with Maria and the children on the steps of the Mirabell Gardens, with the fortress behind them.
